title: How Many People Can One Boss Handle? | Principles of Management Ep 27
description:
How many people can one manager really handle? Chai Corner now has five outlets and thirty people, and all thirty still report straight to Ravi. A new helper waits two days for an answer, a cash mistake goes unseen for a week, and Ravi falls behind every night. In this animated lesson we use Ravi's chai chain to understand span of control, step by step.

You will learn what span of control means (also called span of management: the number of people one manager can supervise well), and why too wide a span breaks down, using the formula V.A. Graicunas published in 1933 in Relationship in Organization: with 2 people a manager handles 6 relationships, with 5 people 100, and with 6 people 222. Then we watch the same thirty people re-arrange on screen into a flat chart with five outlet managers, a tall chart with a narrow span (15 managers, 5 levels) and a flat chart with a wide span (6 managers, 3 levels), and send one message down each to see why tall charts are slow. At work today, we look at the five things that set the right span: the work, skill, guidance, technology and distance, from packers and senior engineers to new nurses, team chats and regional managers. We also look at the human side: too narrow and people feel watched, too wide and nobody gets help.

This is Episode 27 of our Principles of Management series for MBA, BBA and commerce students.
